meta.title: NCR Scam Awareness Guide
meta.description: Illustrated common scam, theft, and safety tactics for international visitors to Delhi and Gurugram, mapped by area.
meta.notes: Only Delhi and Gurugram districts are highlighted/in-scope on this map. Coordinates are [lat, lng] pairs (WGS84, decimal degrees). Boundary polygons are simplified extracts from OpenStreetMap via Nominatim (polygon_threshold=0.005).

tactics.name: Fake "Tourism Office" Redirect
tactics.summary: A friendly stranger strikes up conversation near a landmark and offers a free rickshaw tour, then leads visitors to an unofficial travel agency displaying a fake "Ministry of Tourism" sign that pressures them into an overpriced multi-day package.
tactics.avoid: Book tours only through your hotel or a pre-vetted operator. Real government tourism offices don't recruit customers on the street.

tactics.name: "Your Train Is Cancelled" Redirect
tactics.summary: Someone claims the platform is closed, your train is cancelled, or election/monsoon disruptions block the route, then guides travelers away from the station to a private travel agency instead.
tactics.avoid: Check train status only on the official IRCTC app or with uniformed railway staff at the information counter inside the station.

tactics.name: Rigged Taxi Meter / Long Route
tactics.summary: Drivers take a deliberately roundabout route, claim the meter is broken, or simply demand a high flat fare once the ride is already underway.
tactics.avoid: Use the official prepaid taxi counter or a ride-hailing app, and follow the route on your own phone's map.

tactics.name: Street "Ear Cleaning" Health Scam
tactics.summary: A self-described ear specialist offers a free inspection, then inserts something into the ear and demands escalating cash payments to stop.
tactics.avoid: Politely decline all unsolicited medical, grooming, or massage offers from strangers on the street.

tactics.name: Gem / Carpet "Investment" Scam
tactics.summary: A shop convinces a traveler that gems, carpets, or spices bought cheaply can be resold for a large profit back home, then arranges a "shipping" deal for goods that never arrive or are worthless.
tactics.avoid: Never buy anything framed as a resale investment — only pay for what you can personally inspect and carry.

tactics.name: Currency Short-Counting
tactics.summary: A vendor or money changer counts change quickly and hands back less than owed, or swaps a large note for a smaller one during a distracting handoff.
tactics.avoid: Count all cash slowly and openly before completing a transaction, and count it again afterward.

tactics.name: Crowd Pickpocketing
tactics.summary: In dense markets, pickpockets work in pairs — one creates a bump or distraction while another lifts a wallet or phone from a bag or pocket.
tactics.avoid: Keep valuables in a zipped front pocket or money belt, and keep bags closed and worn to the front in crowds.

tactics.name: Distraction Bag-Snatching Team
tactics.summary: A group distracts a visitor — asking for directions, offering photos, or a staged spill — while an accomplice grabs an unattended bag or phone off a table.
tactics.avoid: Never leave a bag or phone unattended on a table or chair, even for a moment.

tactics.name: Aggressive Begging / Child Gangs
tactics.summary: Groups of children, often directed by adults who take most of what is collected, surround visitors, grab at clothing or arms, and don't back off easily when refused.
tactics.avoid: Keep walking calmly toward a shop or crowd rather than stopping to argue; avoid handing out cash directly.

tactics.name: Nightlife Area Harassment
tactics.summary: Around bar streets late at night, groups of men or persistent beggars can surround and closely follow visitors, escalating if ignored for too long.
tactics.avoid: Travel in a group after dark, keep a ride-hailing app ready, and leave promptly if you feel surrounded.
